$comment: Network egress policy, applied by the egress proxy to every connection a tool (or the harness) makes; see docs/design/egress-proxy.md. Everything is refused unless something allows it: the engagement a tool call runs under (inside its testing window), the tool's egress block in tools.json, or an Allow rule here. Deny rules always win. allowedPorts: ports a connection may use unless a tool's egress block names its own. blockNonPublicAddresses: refuse names that resolve to private, loopback, link-local (cloud metadata) or other non-public addresses, unless a cidr Allow rule covers the address. Each rule: id (stable), action (Allow | Deny), match.type (domain = the domain and its subdomains | exact = that host only | regex = the whole host, anchored with ^ and $ | cidr = the resolved address), match.value, optional appliesTo (tool function names, or harness:llm for the harness's own LLM calls; empty means everyone) and description.

rules.description: Cloud instance metadata services hand out credentials; nothing should reach them, even if a cidr rule would allow it.
Paste sites and tunnelling services are common exfiltration routes, so they're refused even if an engagement lists them.
